ingredients.changeReason: A 1:1 gluten-free blend with xanthan gum is the only swap that keeps the dough workable. Expect a wetter dough than the original.
ingredients.alternative: Equal parts white rice flour, tapioca starch and sorghum, plus 1 tsp xanthan gum per cup

ingredients.changeReason: Scaled to roughly 85 percent of linear because gluten-free dough proofs faster and over-proofing collapses the crumb.
Scaled with the yeast to keep the ratio intact.
Rice and tapioca starches absorb more water than wheat flour, so hydration goes up or the crumb reads dry.
Acid strengthens the protein network that gluten would normally build, which is what stops the loaf collapsing as it cools.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.original_note: Stir until a shaggy dough forms.
steps.updated_note: Gluten-free dough will look like a thick batter rather than a shaggy dough. That is correct. Do not add flour to firm it up.

steps.title: First rise
steps.updated_note: Cut the rise to 60 to 90 minutes. There is no gluten to develop, so extra time only exhausts the yeast.

steps.title: Bake
steps.updated_note: Drop the oven to 450°F and bake 35 to 40 minutes. Gluten-free browns faster than it sets, so a hot oven gives you a dark crust over a raw centre.

steps.title: Cool
steps.updated_note: Cool completely, at least 2 hours. Slicing a warm gluten-free loaf is the single most common cause of a gummy crumb.

explanations: The vinegar is doing structural work, not flavour work. You will not taste it in the finished loaf.
Dropping the oven 25 degrees and extending the bake is the trade that makes the centre set before the crust burns.
Gluten-free bread stales faster. Slice and freeze what you will not eat in two days.
